observations: Red/black portable generator with 'KEMAGE' logo clearly visible on front panel and control panel (photo 0)
Control panel shows a voltmeter, circuit breaker switches, two AC 220V sockets, a DC 12V outlet, and an engine on/off switch
Unit sits on a two-wheel trolley frame with red wheels, has carrying handles, and a visible 12V battery mounted underneath for electric start
Fuel tank cap and a small data/warning sticker are visible on top but the text is too small/unreadable to confirm capacity or specs
Background shows unrelated boxed appliances and a 'Stantech Electronics' watermark, suggesting this may be a shop/catalog photo rather than a photo of the specific unit being sold
No visible rating plate showing kVA, wattage, or serial number legible in the image

claims.evidence: Brand 'KEMAGE' is readable in photo 0, but no kVA rating plate or sticker is legible in the image to confirm 8.5kva
No way to confirm age or usage hours from a single static photo; no run-time meter or dated proof shown
Internal winding/coil is not visible in any photo; this claim cannot be checked without opening the unit or seeing a manufacturer spec sheet
No warranty card, receipt, or proof-of-purchase shown in the photo

risks.risk: Actual output capacity (kVA) may differ from claimed 8.5kva, which significantly changes price bracket
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the rating plate/sticker on the generator body showing kVA/wattage and model number
risks.if_unproven: priced as unknown/lowest plausible capacity for a Kemage-branded unit of this size

risks.risk: Generator may not start or run; no load test shown
risks.proof: Video clip of the generator starting and running under load with visible voltmeter reading

risks.risk: Coil material (copper vs aluminum) cannot be verified visually and affects longevity/value
risks.proof: Manufacturer spec sheet or photo of coil winding during an open inspection
risks.if_unproven: priced as standard/unverified winding, not premium copper

risks.risk: Photo may be a generic catalog/stock image rather than the actual unit for sale, masking true condition (scratches, rust, wear, missing parts)
risks.proof: Fresh photos of the actual unit from multiple angles with timestamp or handwritten seller note visible
risks.if_unproven: priced as used with unknown cosmetic condition, worst case

risks.risk: Claimed '4 months use' and 'on warranty' cannot be substantiated, affecting resale value expectations
risks.proof: Photo of purchase receipt, warranty card, or box with visible purchase date
risks.if_unproven: priced as used with no warranty

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the rating plate/sticker showing kVA, model number, and serial number
Video of the generator starting and running under some load, showing the voltmeter
Photo of the purchase receipt or warranty card showing purchase date
Additional photos of the unit from other angles (sides, rear, underside) showing actual cosmetic condition
response.reason: The brand is identifiable but the kVA rating that sets the price bracket is not legible in the photo, and all condition/usage/warranty claims are unverifiable from a single catalog-style image, so even a worst-case price cannot be anchored without a clear capacity label shot.
